slides.purpose: Present the incomplete three-door choice; ask whether two remaining doors imply equal chances.
slides.successCheck: State what was seen without assuming the host always reveals a goat.
slides.representation: Static unmarked doors preserve the unanswered question; no sampling or reveal gate.

slides.purpose: Fix uniform prize placement, an independent initial choice, an informed always-goat host and an always-offered switch.
slides.successCheck: Identify the rules used in the next calculation.
slides.representation: A concise static rule diagram is sufficient; no unknown result is animated.
slides.interaction: Static rule declaration; fair tie-breaking is reserved for the concrete experiment.

slides.purpose: Enumerate all three prize locations; show the opened door and switching result for each.
slides.successCheck: Explain why both initially wrong choices become wins and obtain 2/3.
slides.representation: Read the worked explanation before the live ledger, in visual and DOM order. Three explicit door cases; the live ledger splits each equally likely prize case into two equal probability units. These six units are a calculation, not six observed games.
slides.interaction: Change initial door or host policy; the same case identities and retained units update. Initial/reset is informed, zero samples, complete stage 3. Unsupported snapshots are rejected atomically; selected inputs survive navigation and restoration.

slides.purpose: Return to the opening and distinguish seeing a goat once from a host who always reveals goats.
slides.successCheck: Explain why the valid 2/3 argument needs rules absent from the opening.
slides.representation: Side-by-side always-goat versus accidental-goat procedures, without asserting a new answer.
slides.interaction: Static transition; the changed-rule calculation follows immediately.

slides.purpose: Use the same six equal probability units; blind random opening retains two initially correct units and one per initially wrong prize location.
slides.successCheck: Identify the two excluded prize reveals and derive 2/4=1/2 from the remaining four units.
slides.representation: Read the worked explanation before the live ledger, in visual and DOM order. Visible retained and crossed-out units alongside an explicit per-row reason; the denominator is the number of remaining equal units.
slides.interaction: Switch host policy while holding initial choice fixed to compare 4/6=2/3 with 2/4=1/2. Reset is blind, zero samples, stage 3; preserve input and synchronize added feedback. Sampling remains optional.

slides.purpose: Optionally restrict to door 2 being opened under an informed host who prefers door 2 whenever allowed.
slides.successCheck: Reconstruct the retained prize cases 1 and 3, derive 1/2, and distinguish this subset from overall switching success 2/3.
slides.representation: A static three-case table with explicit opened doors supplies the complete changed-rule deduction; no t parameter or likelihood vocabulary is required.
slides.interaction: Static worked transfer: the existing experiment conditions on any goat reveal and cannot simulate this numbered-door restriction. Return explicitly to compare.

slides.purpose: Answer the opening by comparing guaranteed-goat and accidental-goat procedures.
slides.successCheck: Explain why eliminating a door does not by itself make the two remaining possibilities equally likely.
slides.representation: A compact comparison of which initially wrong games survive; no new formula or prerequisite.
slides.interaction: Static synthesis; optional numbered-door branch is unnecessary for this payoff.
